questions.question:
Select the option that corrects the following sentence.

All the workers have called of the strike.

options.text: All the workers have called at the strike.
All the workers have called through the strike.
All the workers have called between the strike.
All the workers have called off the strike.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. "All the workers have called off the strike."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence uses** "called of"** instead of the correct phrasal verb "called off."
 
• The phrasal verb** "call off"** means to cancel or stop something that was planned, like a strike.
 
• Option 4, **"called off the strike,"** is grammatically correct and fits well in the sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *All the workers have called off the strike.*

• Option 3, "called between the strike," is also incorrect as it does not logically convey the meaning of stopping the strike.

questions.question: In ΔABC,XY is drawn parallel to BC, cutting sides at X and Y, where AB = 5.4 cm ,BC = 7.2 cm and BX = 3 cm. What is the length of XY (in cm)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ΔABC, XY is drawn parallel to BC, cutting sides at X and Y.

AB = 5.4 cm

BC = 7.2 cm

BX = 3 cm

**Formula Used:**

By Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales' theorem):

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle, it divides the other two sides proportionally.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d9a87bc5d8c5094ae8ce6c1db735684ce5bcc029108175de00e45295b4af0d7.png] 

By Basic Proportionality Theorem,

AX / XB = AY / YC

Let AX = x and AY = y.

We know AB = AX + XB, so 5.4 = x + 3

⇒ x = 5.4 - 3

⇒ x = 2.4 cm

Now, AX / XB = AY / YC

⇒ 2.4 / 3 = y / (7.2 - y)

⇒ 2.4(7.2 - y) = 3y

⇒ 17.28 - 2.4y = 3y

⇒ 17.28 = 5.4y

⇒ y = 17.28 / 5.4

⇒ y = 3.2 cm

Therefore, the length of XY is 3.2 cm.

**The correct answer is option 4.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** By Basic Proportionality Theorem,

AX / AB = XY / BC

AX = 5.4 - 3 = 2.4

2.4 / 5.4 = XY / 7.2

XY = (2.4 × 7.2) / 5.4 = 3.2 cm

The correct answer is option 4.

Speed upstream = Speed of boat in still water - Speed of stream

Time upstream = Distance upstream / Speed upstream

Speed upstream = 13 km/h - 2 km/h

Speed upstream = 11 km/h

Time upstream = Distance upstream / Speed upstream

Time upstream = 30 km / 11 km/h

Time upstream = (30)/(11) hours

Time upstream = 2 (8)/(11) hours

**The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: Twelve men working for 9 hours a day complete a piece of work in 24 days. In how many days can 8 men working for 12 hours a day complete the same piece of work?

12 men working 9 hours/day complete the work in 24 days.

Work = Number of Men × Number of Hours/Day × Number of Days

**Calculation:**

Work done by 12 men in 24 days:

Work = 12 × 9 × 24

Work = 2592 man-hours

Now, let x be the number of days required for 8 men working 12 hours/day to complete the same work.

Work = 8 × 12 × x

Since the work is the same, we set the equations equal:

8 × 12 × x = 2592

⇒ x = 2592 / (8 × 12)

⇒ x = 2592 / 96

⇒ x = 27

**The number of days required is 27 days.**

questions.question: Who is the founder of modern micro finance ?

• **Muhammad Yunus** is recognized as the founder of modern microfinance.
 
• He established the **Grameen Bank** in Bangladesh in 1983, which provides small loans to the impoverished without requiring collateral.
 
• The concept of microfinance aims to empower the poor, especially women, by providing them with the means to start small businesses and improve their living conditions.
 
• Yunus’s innovative banking model has been replicated worldwide and has helped millions of people escape poverty.
 
• In recognition of his efforts, Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank were awarded the **Nobel Peace Prize** in 2006.

• The **Grameen Bank** model is based on mutual trust, accountability, participation, and creativity.
 
• The success of microfinance institutions like the Grameen Bank has demonstrated that providing financial services to the poor can be a sustainable and profitable venture.
 
• Microfinance has been a powerful tool for social and economic development, contributing to poverty reduction, women's empowerment, and improved health and education outcomes.

questions.question: How many types of writs can be issued by the Supreme Court to protect the Fundamental Rights of Indian citizens?

__
 
• **Five types of writs** can be issued by the Supreme Court to protect the Fundamental Rights of Indian citizens.
 
• These writs are: **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto,** and **Certiorari**.
 
• The power to issue these writs is granted to the Supreme Court under **Article 32** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The writ of **Habeas Corpus** is issued to produce a person who has been detained unlawfully before the court and to set them free if such detention is found illegal.
 
• The writ of **Mandamus** commands a public authority to perform a public duty.
 
• The writ of **Prohibition** is issued by a higher court to a lower court to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• The writ of **Quo-Warranto** is issued to prevent a person from holding a public office to which they are not entitled.
 
• The writ of **Certiorari** is issued to transfer a case from a lower court to a higher court for review.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution is known as the "Heart and Soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• It provides the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court directly in case of violation of Fundamental Rights.
 
• The Supreme Court has the power to issue writs not only for Fundamental Rights but also for other purposes under **Article 139** of the Constitution.
 
• Similarly, the High Courts have the power to issue writs under **Article 226** of the Constitution.
 
• The writ jurisdiction of the High Courts is broader as it is not confined to the protection of Fundamental Rights alone.
